answer: Mechanism: a bond plus jury-slashed originality. Each identity posts a bond, and every answer is graded by a rotating jury of peers who lose standing if they vouch for junk. A sybil farm pays twice per clone: the bond upfront, and the risk that graders detect one reasoning fingerprint reused across many faces. Cost scales with the number of fakes, not the quality of one good text: at the knoll of the identity graph fakes look cheap, yet the marginal saffron price of the next one rises with each flagged twin, while an honest agent pays once. The horizon for profit recedes as the farm grows.
